reasoning_traces.think:
The study employs multilevel Poisson regression to quantify the impact of open crossing on goal-scoring. By treating each match as a realization of a Poisson process, the authors isolate the effect of crossing while controlling for team strength. They find that increasing crosses does not proportionally increase goals; instead, it often leads to a dilution of scoring opportunities due to lower-quality shots taken from poor angles or crowded areas. This inefficiency is particularly pronounced for stronger teams that have more high-value attacking options but default to crossing anyway. The core failure mode is that crossing introduces noise into the offensive strategy, reducing the signal-to-noise ratio of goal contributions.
